{{Short description|Functional analysis operator}}
In [[functional analysis]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''Favard operators''' are defined by:

:<math>[\mathcal{F}_n(f)](x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n\pi}} \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty {\exp{\left({-n {\left({\frac{k}{n}-x}\right)}^2 }\right)} f\left(\frac{k}{n}\right)}</math>

where <math>x\in\mathbb{R}</math>, <math>n\in\mathbb{N}</math>. They are named after [[Jean Favard]].

==Generalizations==
A common generalization is:
:<math>[\mathcal{F}_n(f)](x) = \frac{1}{n\gamma_n\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty {\exp{\left({\frac{-1}{2\gamma_n^2} {\left({\frac{k}{n}-x}\right)}^2 }\right)} f\left(\frac{k}{n}\right)}</math>

where <math>(\gamma_n)_{n=1}^\infty</math> is a positive sequence that [[Limit of a sequence|converges]] to 0.<ref name="Nowak">{{cite journal|last=Nowak|first=Grzegorz|author2=Aneta Sikorska-Nowak|date=14 November 2007|title=On the generalized Favard–Kantorovich and Favard–Durrmeyer operators in exponential function spaces|url=https://eudml.org/doc/128662|journal=Journal of Inequalities and Applications|volume=2007|page=075142 |doi=10.1155/2007/75142|doi-access=free}}</ref> This reduces to the classical Favard operators when <math>\gamma_n^2=1/(2n)</math>.

==References==
*{{cite journal| last=Favard | first=Jean | authorlink=Jean Favard | year=1944 | title=Sur les multiplicateurs d'interpolation | journal=Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées | volume=23 | issue=9 | pages=219–247|language=fr |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k9704240z/f235.item}} This paper also discussed [[Szász–Mirakyan operator]]s, which is why Favard is sometimes credited with their development (e.g. Favard–Szász operators).
